items.title: Uniform periodic, infinite, and Dirichlet grid conventions
items.statement: For N≥2 and h,k>0, define the periodic, infinite, and finite-interval uniform grids, with finite nodes x_j=jh and L=Nh, weighted norms, interior and edge inner products, centered/one-sided differences, and second differences on their stated index sets.
items.axiom_base: Definition only; no choice axiom is used.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3–§6.6, PDF pp. 85–104: uniform wave/advection grids, grid differences, and weighted mesh norms.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete 5-page PDF, pp. 1–4: uniform-grid differences and Fourier-mode symbols.

items.title: Periodic advection schemes and the finite-interval upwind row
items.statement: For u_t+a u_x=0 with a>0, mesh h,k>0, and ν=ak/h, define periodic or infinite-grid upwind, downwind, centered, Lax–Friedrichs, and Lax–Wendroff updates by their stated three-point stencils; set U_j^0=u_0(jh) and reduce periodic indices modulo N. For a<0 reflect j↦−j. On a finite interval define only the upwind branch with U_0^n=g(t_n) at the inflow, compatible initial row U_j^0=u_0(jh), j=1,…,N, and no prescribed value at the outflow.
items.axiom_base: Definition only; no choice axiom is used.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.5–§6.6, PDF pp. 97–104: linear transport, inflow boundary data, and the explicit upwind rows.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lectures 15 and 18
references.locator: Lecture 15, complete PDF pp. 1–4: upwind, downwind, centered, Lax–Friedrichs, and Lax–Wendroff formulas. Its u_t=c u_x convention is reflected to the present u_t+a u_x=0 convention.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 18, Boundary Conditions for Advection
references.locator: Complete 3-page PDF, pp. 1–2: upwind inflow/outflow handling and separate numerical boundary data for Lax–Friedrichs/Lax–Wendroff.

items.title: Centered leapfrog wave recurrence with Dirichlet and periodic rows
items.statement: For a real wave grid with c,h,k>0 and ν=ck/h, prescribe displacement U^0 and discrete initial velocity V^0 and set U^1=U^0+kV^0. Define the centered two-step recurrence on periodic or homogeneous Dirichlet rows, with both initial rows and boundary values explicit; Fourier analysis uses the complex-linear extension.
items.axiom_base: Definition only; no choice axiom is used.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3–§6.4, PDF pp. 85–96: centered explicit wave recurrence, initial/boundary rows, and Fourier analysis.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete 5-page PDF, pp. 1–4: centered second-order spatial stencil and explicit time update; used as a difference-method comparison, not as a wave-energy proof.

items.title: One-dimensional discrete summation by parts with boundary terms
items.statement: For complex finite-interval grid functions, the interior inner product and centered second difference satisfy ⟨u,−Δ_hv⟩_h=⟨D_+u,D_+v⟩_{e,h}+u_0 overline((D_+v)_0)−u_N overline((D_-v)_N). Zero endpoints remove the boundary terms and give self-adjoint nonnegativity.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof is a finite telescoping sum.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3, PDF pp. 85–89: the finite-grid summation-by-parts identity and homogeneous Dirichlet energy terms.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.6, PDF pp. 99–101: one-sided differences and boundary flux terms for inflow transport.

items.title: A finite-grid Poincare inequality for zero endpoint values
items.statement: For a complex grid function with zero endpoint values on a uniform interval L=Nh, the weighted interior norm satisfies ‖w‖_h≤L‖D_+w‖_{e,h}.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite sums and exact real algebra.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3, PDF pp. 87–89: the finite-grid Poincare–Friedrichs estimate used to discuss the endpoint energy norm.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.6, PDF pp. 100–101: the telescoping boundary-grid energy calculation.

items.title: Smooth consistency orders for the five periodic advection stencils
items.statement: For fixed nonzero a and a C^6 periodic solution of u_t+a u_x=0 with bounded derivatives, and two-sided k/h bounds, the sign-selected upwind, downwind, centered and Lax–Friedrichs residuals are O(h), while Lax–Wendroff is O(h²).
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses Taylor remainders and the classical translation solution.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.6, PDF pp. 99–104: upwind truncation error and the exact inflow/outflow setup.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 1–4: Taylor consistency orders for upwind, downwind, centered, and Lax–Wendroff; the Lax–Friedrichs exercise is completed locally with the two-sided k/h condition.

items.title: Coercive discrete energy for the Dirichlet leapfrog wave scheme
items.statement: For the real homogeneous-Dirichlet leapfrog recurrence with fixed c>0 and 0<ν=ck/h<1, the displayed adjacent-level energy is conserved and bounds the discrete velocity and averaged spatial gradient with coefficients 1−ν² and c². For fixed c,L and ν≤ν₀<1 it uniformly controls the interior state and velocity over meshes.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite grid sums and exact real arithmetic.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3, PDF pp. 85–89: discrete wave-energy identity, discrete summation by parts, positivity under cΔt/Δx≤1, and loss of mesh-uniform coercivity at equality.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 1–4: advection comparison only; no discrete second-order wave-energy proof is imported.

items.title: Amplification symbols for periodic scalar advection stencils
items.statement: On an N-point periodic grid, for z=e^{2πiℓ/N}, C=Re z, S=Im z, and ν=ak/h with a>0, the five one-step factors are g_up=1−ν+νz^{-1}, g_down=1+ν−νz, g_center=1−iνS, g_LF=C−iνS, and g_LW=1−ν²(1−C)−iνS. Their squared moduli are respectively 1−2ν(1−ν)(1−C), 1+2ν(1+ν)(1−C), 1+ν²S², 1−(1−ν²)S², and 1−ν²(1−ν²)(1−C)².
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite Fourier modes and complex arithmetic.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.4, PDF pp. 91–96: Fourier reduction of the centered wave recurrence; §6.6, PDF pp. 99–104: upwind amplification and CFL analysis.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 2–4: amplification factors for upwind, downwind, centered, Lax–Friedrichs, and Lax–Wendroff; signs are reflected to u_t+a u_x=0.

items.title: Periodic leapfrog amplification, finite-time bounds, and the Nyquist endpoint
items.statement: On a periodic grid of length L=Nh, with ν=ck/h and Fourier coefficient w_ℓ for mode ℓ, each centered leapfrog mode satisfies w_ℓ^{n+1}−2(1−2ν²sin²(πℓ/N))w_ℓ^n+w_ℓ^{n−1}=0. For 0<ν≤ν₀<1, nonconstant roots are distinct and lie on the unit circle and the finite-time grid norm obeys ‖U^n‖≤(1+ν₀/√(1−ν₀²))‖U^0‖+t_n‖V^0‖; the mean mode is w₀^n=w₀^0+t_n V̂₀^0. At ν=1 with even N the Nyquist mode has repeated root −1 and generalized component absent exactly when w^1=−w^0; arbitrary starts have no uniform endpoint power bound.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite Fourier modes and a finite root recurrence.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.4, PDF pp. 91–96: exact periodic wave characteristic roots, practical stability estimates, and the strict CFL restriction; §6.3, PDF pp. 87–89: endpoint loss of a mesh-uniform energy coercivity constant.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3, PDF pp. 85–89: finite-grid centered wave energy identity and the equality endpoint distinction.

items.title: Scheme-specific periodic power stability for scalar advection
items.statement: On periodic grids with a>0, upwind powers are contractions for 0≤ν≤1, and Lax–Friedrichs and Lax–Wendroff powers are contractions for |ν|≤1. Downwind powers grow for every ν>0 on any N≥2 grid. Centered powers grow for every ν≠0 when N≥3; for N=2 the centered stencil aliases to the identity. For the reflected a<0 stencils the same conclusions hold with |ν|.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses the finite orthogonal Fourier basis.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.4 and §6.6, PDF pp. 91–104: periodic wave and one-way advection amplification calculations.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 2–4: the four named advection scheme stability calculations and CFL ranges.

items.title: The nearest-neighbor CFL condition is necessary but not sufficient
items.statement: Under a fixed strict violation ak/h≥1+ε, a homogeneous explicit nearest-neighbor update fails to converge in sampled maximum error from one fixed smooth compact datum. Independently, for fixed-period centered periodic grids N_q=4q with ak_q/h_q=1/2, the z=i mode makes finite-time power norms unbounded for every fixed T.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the argument uses finite stencil dependence and the exact translation solution.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.6, PDF pp. 99–104: CFL and domain-of-dependence context for one-way advection.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 1–2: characteristic direction, the upwind CFL condition, and the centered instability despite the same finite-difference setting.

items.title: The Nyquist mode at and beyond the leapfrog CFL endpoint
items.statement: For an even periodic grid, the centered leapfrog Nyquist mode has a repeated root −1 at ν=1 and a growing root when ν>1; the usual modified wave energy is semidefinite at ν=1 and indefinite for ν>1.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the verification is a finite Fourier-mode calculation.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §6.3–§6.4, PDF pp. 87–96: strict wave-energy coercivity and the periodic explicit-wave root calculation.

items.title: Upwind damping versus downwind growth on a periodic grid
items.statement: On a four-point periodic grid with ν=1/2, the Fourier mode z=i has upwind multiplier of modulus 1/√2 and downwind multiplier of modulus √(5/2).
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the verification is a finite complex-arithmetic calculation.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 2–3: upwind conditional stability and downwind instability; the present advection sign convention is the reflected stencil.

items.title: Centered advection is consistent and unstable under the CFL bound
items.statement: For the fixed-period family N_q=4q, h_q=P/N_q and k_q=h_q/(2a), centered advection has O(h_q) residual on every fixed smooth admissible solution, while the mode ℓ=q has z=i and yields unbounded finite-time power norms.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the verification is a finite Fourier-mode calculation.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 15, Finite Difference Methods for the One-Way Wave Equation
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 1–2: centered consistency order and centered instability.

items.title: Grid Fourier stability alone does not instantiate Lax equivalence
items.statement: For periodic upwind updates on different N-point spaces with fixed 0<ν<1, the grid power bounds do not by themselves satisfy the common-Banach-space hypotheses of the Lax equivalence theorem.
items.axiom_base: Dependent Choice is carried because the cited Lax-equivalence supplier assumes DC; no choice axiom is used in the finite-grid calculation.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Finite Difference and Spectral Methods, Chapter 4, §4.2
references.locator: Complete PDF pp. 8–13, §4.2: the common Banach-space Lax-equivalence theorem and its same-norm hypotheses.
